To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we introduce a novel approach to part discovery that learns a decomposition into meaningful parts; 2) we show empirically why previous approaches are unlikely to learn meaningful parts; 3) we propose new metrics for the evaluation of part discovery methods.

(1) the standard evaluation based only on the regression of keypoints does not capture all relevant information about the part discovery task, (2) the use of reconstruction as a proxy task for part discovery is complementary to clustering and can help to alleviate the problem of spatial smearing in pre-trained features, and (3) the use of a contrastive reconstruction loss is crucial to the success of the proposed method, as it encourages the model to find a meaningful decomposition of objects into its parts

(1) the standard evaluation based keypoint regression is not well suited for evaluating part discovery and segmentation, (2) image reconstruction at the pixel level is an important complementary cue to pre-computed features and (3) the proposed unsupervised method for part discovery and segmentation is state of the art in this field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How to learn representations of parts of objects in a self-supervised manner?
unsupervised representation learning at part-level and the following contributions are made: 1. An unsupervised part discovery and segmentation method.

unsupervised part discovery from contrastive reconstruction, and we make three contributions: (i) we propose a set of objectives which can encourage the model to learn to discover meaningful parts of the image, (ii) we introduce new metrics for evaluation, and (iii) we empirically show that reconstruction of pixels can be a complementary cue to pre-computed features, leading to better part segmentation
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we propose a method for discovering parts of objects, and that our method is better than previous methods at discovering parts of objects.
the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of the proposed metrics and also outperforms the existing methods for key-point prediction in terms of the standard metric.
our approach is the first to learn a meaningful part decomposition of objects in a self-supervised manner and that we introduce novel metrics to evaluate part segmentation quality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel unsupervised part discovery approach that can be used for transfer learning.
we show that contrastive reconstruction is a useful proxy to part discovery and we introduce new metrics for evaluation.
we propose an unsuervised part discovery and segmentation method that is able to find meaningful parts that can be used for transfer learning and that can be generalized to fine-grained datasets.
The main takeaway from our work is that

image reconstruction is an important component in learning part representations, especially in the unsupervised setting, and that the standard evaluation of keypoint regression is not a good proxy to part discovery and segmentation.
the quality of part discovery is highly dependent on the choice of proxy tasks, and that pixel-level reconstruction is a promising direction for future work.
the standard approach of using pre-computed features for clustering or reconstruction does not work as well as it could be.
